Widebody Ferrari 458 Comes From Japan With Love
6 photos
Photo: Instagram | libertywalk_toshi
How long has it been since we last wrote about the Ferrari 458? Well, roughly one month, and the previous one to have caught our attention was a Spider that was looking for a new home in the United States of America, with approximately 18,000 miles (29,000 km) on the clock.
This one, on the other hand, is not for sale. And it is not even on the same continent, as it lives pretty much on the other side of the world. The 458 in question is a permanent resident of the Land of the Rising sun, and since it is definitely on the more special side of things, it has caught our attention. Mind you, more special does not necessarily mean prettier, because looks are definitely in the eyes of the beholder, and not everyone will agree that it looks better than the stock one.
At this point, we are tempted to ask you how this Ferrari 458 makes you feel, inviting you to scroll down to the comments box, and drop a few lines. However, we haven’t yet delved into the things that make it quite unique, so we’d better do that. And before we do, we should also mention that the tuner behind this project calls it the LB Silhouette Works Ferrari 458 GT, and as you already know, it is none other than Liberty Walk, with @libertywalk_toshi recently sharing these images on social media.
The caption does not really say anything about this modern-classic, rear mid-engined, and rear-wheel drive Italian supercar, other than what we already told you, and the fact that it “looks pretty cool.” And who am I to say otherwise? The exotic build features the Liberty Walk-signature widebody kit, so it looks a lot more muscular than the OEM one. The front bumper has been reworked, it features some vents flanking the standard headlights, and a quite discreet splitter with blades on the sides.
Photo: Instagram | libertywalk_toshi In this case, the Ferrari 458 Italia in question retains its front hood. The front fenders are a lot wider than before, and so are the rear three-quarter panels, as these, as well as the new side skirts, have come directly from Liberty Walk’s portfolio. Out back, the pictured supercar is home to a new large wing, as well as a different diffuser. And just like the front element, the rear bumper has also been modified, from what we can tell.
The supercar is presented in red, and does not feature that many decals on its body compared to other builds that have come from this tuner’s garage. An adjustable air suspension appears to be part of the makeover. The wheels are also new, and they are wider at the rear. We can see a tiny bit of negative camber, too, for more street cred. So, what’s your take on this modded Ferrari 458 ? Is it a yay in your book? Because it is one one mine!
Before wrapping it up, we have to remind you that the Ferrari 458 features a naturally aspirated 4.5-liter V8 engine behind the passenger compartment. It puts out 562 hp (570 ps/419 kW ) and 398 pound-feet (540 Nm) of torque, and provides unique thrills. The 458 Italia hits 62 mph (100 kph) in 3.4 seconds, identical to the 458 Spider, and the top speed is 202 mph (325 kph), whereas the open-top flavor will do 199 mph (320 kph) flat out.
